Stated Claim / Post Context:
Best of September: Amazon’s largest reserve, new global fund to end FGM, reviving the art of public debate

From a new giant reserve in Colombia's Amazon region to a village that revived India's lost art of public debate: here's our recap of the best and most important pieces of constructive news and stories from September.

Actual Article Body:
Jonathan Widder | Posted on September 30, 2026 |

Photo: Azzedine Rouichi / Unsplash (CC0)

From a new giant reserve in Colombia’s Amazon region to a village that revived India’s lost art of public debate: here’s our recap of the best and most important pieces of constructive news and stories from September.

Just a few days before the end of his term in office, President Gustavo Petro has permanently barred new mining and oil projects from almost half of the Colombian Amazon, creating the Amazon’s largest reserve so far. Existing projects may continue, but no new licences will be granted.

Source: Lyxplanet

The Halo Trust, a mine-clearance charity, announced this week that it has completed its work in Kosovo, saying the land cleared of mines has “paved the way for Kosovo’s recovery.” More than 800,000 people were displaced during the 1998-99 conflict. In the first month after the war, an estimated 150 people were killed or injured by landmines, 71% of them under the age of 24.

Source: Squirrel News

The aim of Her Horizon Fund is to pool $100m from donors to reach a “tipping point” towards ending female genital mutilation within a generation. Advocates warn that while international recognition of FGM as a human rights violation has grown, and countries such as Burkina Faso, the Gambia and Kenya have criminalised the practice, progress remains fragile.

Source: The Guardian

Between June and August, New York City saw 195 shooting incidents, 249 shooting victims and 66 murders – the fewest in recorded history for each category. Major crime dropped by 6.6% citywide in August, with The Bronx leading the decline.

Source: CBS News

Mexico is seeing a sustained decline in homicides, with July marking the lowest monthly average in more than a decade. Daily killings fell to 42.5, continuing a broader downward trend in violent crime, and the January-July average also dropped to its lowest level for that period since 2015.

Source: Mexico News Daily

The Health House by House programme is bringing basic care directly to communities, with 22.8 million home visits carried out between July 2025 and June 2026. More than 21,000 workers are checking vital signs, updating vaccinations and connecting people to specialist care, while the programme builds the health data infrastructure needed for a planned universal health service in 2027.

Source: Mexico Business

Although member states are not affected equally and more men commit suicide than women, suicide rates have dropped across the EU in general. This is largely thanks to cultural conversation prioritising the importance of mental health issues, as well as tangible suicide prevention measures.

Source: Euronews

Although significant differences remain between countries and socio-economic groups, more Europeans are playing sports and exercising more than in 2022. Additionally, many Europeans say physical activity benefits their physical and mental well-being.

Source: Euronews

The Ellinikon will transform the 620-hectare site into a new coastal district centred around one of Europe’s largest urban parks, with more than 30,000 trees and around three million shrubs covering 70% of the area in greenery.

Source: Euronews

Saudi Arabia’s National Greening Programme has been recognised by the UN as a World Restoration Flagship, following efforts to restore degraded land and revive native ecosystems. The initiative has planted more than 159 million trees, restored nearly one million hectares of habitat, and helped reintroduce species including the gazelle, ibex and Arabian oryx. It has also established a national framework to tackle drought, desertification and climate change.

Source: Decade On Restoration
